To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) undergraduates, graduate students, and faculty all rated the importance of a research study more highly when the article included both an effect size and a comment about its magnitude, and 2) undergraduates, but not graduate students or faculty, rated the importance of the study higher when an effect size was included without a comment about its size.

(a) the presence of an effect size and a comment on the size of the effect size in a journal article influences readers' perceptions of the importance of the results; (b) the presence of a comment on the effect size influences perceptions of importance more than the presence of an actual effect size; and (c) the influence of the comment on the effect sizes is greater for undergraduates than for graduate students and faculty.

(1) undergraduates are more influenced than graduate students and faculty by inclusion of effect sizes and comments about effect sizes; and (2) comments are more influential than effect sizes in influencing undergraduates, but effect sizes are equally influential as comments for graduate students and faculty.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how readers of journal articles interpret the results presented.
the influence of effect sizes and comments about effect sizes on readers' perceptions about research results.
the effect of effect sizes and comments about effect size on readers' perception of research results' significance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
including effect sizes and comments about their magnitude is a good idea, but it is not necessary.
effect size information is not the problem; it is the commentary about the effect that is misleading.
the inclusion of effect size information and the inclusion of a comment about the effect size are two different things, and that the latter is much more important than the former.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
effect size information is useful for the readers and the reviewers, and it is important to have the effect size in the paper.
the inclusion of effect size comments, but not effect sizes per se, can influence the perception of research results' impact.
the effect size itself is not as important as the commentary on the size of the effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect size and the comment are not independent.
it is not the effect size that misleads readers, but rather the commentary that accompanies the effect size.
effect size inclusion is important, but the effect of including effect sizes is moderated by the presence of commentary on the effect size.
